headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and shell-capable pairing: Goose can alter workspace state while marker is read-only, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose has shared_state_with_other_instances via filesystem and can read/write the user filesystem, so it may ingest marker-produced files as instructions. marker is document-processing and may emit attacker-controlled document text into shared outputs. This is not provably blocked, but the bridge is filesystem-based rather than an always-on parser hijack.
conditions: IF Goose reads marker-generated files from the shared workspace as prompts or instructions
IF marker outputs untrusted document text into files Goose later processes
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Require explicit human review before Goose reads marker outputs
Prefix marker outputs with non-executable metadata headers
Use read-only mounts for marker output directories
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad network egress, so sensitive workspace contents can leave the machine if it forwards them to configured providers. marker has no filesystem read or network egress, so the main leakage path is one-way from Goose, not reciprocal. Shared workspace makes the exposure plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Goose is pointed at files containing secrets or regulated data
IF Goose sends those files to configured model providers or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared cwd
Disable network egress for Goose when handling sensitive files
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for marker
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state, while marker cannot write, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is Goose acting on shared files that marker reads or produces. The pair lacks symmetric mutable access, so conflict blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF Goose and marker are both pointed at the same git working tree
IF Goose commits or rewrites files while marker is generating documents
mitigations: Run marker on a copy of the workspace
Have Goose commit only after marker finishes
Use git branches per agent
Lock the working tree during writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level file locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on tool outputs and modify git state, so if marker-produced text is treated as authoritative, Goose may propagate errors into files or commits. marker is document-processing and may generate structured but unverified content. The pair therefore has a default path where A's output becomes B's input without a verification gate.
conditions: IF Goose consumes marker output as factual input without verification
IF Goose uses that output to edit files or create commits
mitigations: Require a human verification step before Goose acts on marker output
Compare marker output against source documents
Limit Goose to draft-only edits
Keep marker outputs in a review folder
requires-engineering: add schema validation for marker outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is not provable from the profiles alone. Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens, while marker exposes no such data classes; the only cited compliance concern is potential handling of sensitive workspace data by Goose, not a documented policy breach by marker.
conditions: IF Goose processes regulated data under a provider or extension policy that forbids it
IF marker outputs are stored under a retention policy different from Goose's workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose sessions
Review provider and extension retention settings
Store marker outputs in a separate retention bucket
Document data-class handling for both agents
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
